ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within rectangle $ABCD$, the bisector of $\angle BCD$ intersects side $AD$ at point $E$, the bisector of $\angle AEC$ intersects the extended line of side $CB$ at point $G$ and intersects side $AB$ at point $F$. If $AB = 3\sqrt{2}$ and $AF = 2BF$, then what is the length of $GB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From rectangle $ABCD$, the angle bisector of $\angle BCD$, CE, intersects AD at E; \\
$\therefore CD=AB=3\sqrt{2}$, $\angle DCE=\angle BCE=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore CD=DE=3\sqrt{2}$, \\
From right triangle CDE, \\
$\therefore CE=\sqrt{CD^2+DE^2}=6$, \\
Also, the angle bisector of $\angle AEC$, EG, intersects AB at point F, \\
$\therefore \angle AEG=\angle CEG$, \\
Since AD$\parallel$BC, \\
$\therefore \angle G=\angle AEG$, \\
$\therefore \angle CEG=\angle G$, \\
$\therefore CG=CE=6$, \\
Since $\angle G=\angle AEF$, $\angle AFE=\angle BFG$, \\
$\therefore \triangle AEF\sim \triangle BGF$, \\
$\therefore \frac{GB}{AE}=\frac{FG}{EF}=\frac{FB}{AF}=\frac{BF}{2BF}=\frac{1}{2}$, \\
Let $BG=x$, then $AE=2x$, thus $BC=AD=3\sqrt{2}+2x$, \\
Because $CG=BC+BG$, \\
$\therefore 6=3\sqrt{2}+2x+x$, solving for $x$ gives $x=\boxed{2-\sqrt{2}}$.
